Algebra I · Lesson 1.4

Expressions

Solve this lesson, free →All lessons

An expression is a set of instructions for doing a calculation. When an expression contains a letter (called a variable), that letter can represent any number. Because of this, a single algebraic expression works for infinitely many cases instead of just one.

Problem
A print shop charges the same way no matter how many posters you order. One poster costs $12$12, two cost $19$19, and three cost $26$26. Each extra poster adds the same amount, and there is a one-time setup charge baked into every order. What does an order of 1010 posters cost, in dollars?
Show a hint
  • From 1 poster to 2, and from 2 to 3, the price climbs by the same fixed step. Find that step first.
  • Once you know the per-poster step, work backward to the setup charge hiding inside the price of one poster.
Show the full solution
Each new poster adds 19−12=719−12=7 dollars, so ten posters cost 7070 for printing. One poster costs 1212, which is 77 for the poster plus 55 of setup, so the setup is 55 and every order is 5+7p5+7p. At p=10p=10 that is 5+70=755+70=75​.
Key idea
A variable is a letter that represents a number. An expression is a set of instructions for doing a calculation, and it may contain variables. In the last problem the 55 is a fixed setup charge and the 77 is the rate per poster, so 5+7p5+7p gives the price of an order of any size. An expression names a value and contains no equals sign. An equation contains one.
Problem
An expression splits into pieces wherever a ++ or a −− sign falls between them, and each piece is called a term. Someone writes 8−3x+5xy+y=48−3x+5xy+y=4. Counting only what sits to the left of the equals sign, how many terms does that expression have?
Show a hint
  • Slice the expression at every ++ and every −−. Each slice is one term, and the leading 88 counts.
Show the full solution
Cutting at each ++ and −− gives 88, −3x−3x, 5xy5xy, and yy, which is 44​ terms. The minus stays on the 3x3x, and the leading 88 counts as a term even though nothing sits in front of it.
Key idea
The terms of an expression are the pieces separated by ++ and −−, and each sign belongs to the term that follows it. This follows from 1.2 and 1.3, where subtracting a number is adding its opposite. So 8−3x8−3x is 8+(−3x)8+(−3x), and the term is −3x−3x, including the minus sign. A term with no variable, like the 88, is a constant term. Keeping the sign attached to its term lets you reorder a chain of terms without changing its value.
Problem
The coefficient of a term is its numerical factor, and it carries the sign sitting in front of it. In the expression 10−6w10−6w, what is the coefficient of ww?
Show a hint
  • Subtracting 6w6w is adding −6w−6w, so the sign in front travels with the number multiplying ww.
Show the full solution
The term holding ww is −6w−6w, so its numerical factor is −6−6​. The minus in front belongs to the term, so answering 66 drops the sign.
Problem
Two expressions look almost the same but do very different things. Writing 4n4n means 44 times nn, while 4+n4+n means 44 plus nn. When n=3n=3, how much larger is 4n4n than 4+n4+n?
Show a hint
  • 4n4n is a product and 4+n4+n is a sum. Evaluate each at n=3n=3 before comparing.
  • The little gap between the 44 and the nn is doing all the work. No sign there means multiply, a plus sign means add.
Show the full solution
At n=3n=3, the product 4n=4⋅3=124n=4⋅3=12 and the sum 4+n=4+3=74+n=4+3=7, so the product runs ahead by 12−7=512−7=5​. The gap between the 44 and the nn means multiply, which is easy to read as a plus.
Key idea
Terms are the pieces separated by ++ and −−. Factors are the pieces multiplied together inside a single term, and the coefficient is the numeric factor. So 4n4n is one term with two factors, 44 and nn, while 4+n4+n is two terms. These get confused because the multiplication in 4n4n has no symbol to mark it, so both forms look like a number followed by a letter.
Problem
At a fair, each ride costs $3$3 and each game costs $5$5. A single expression, 3r+5g3r+5g, gives the total spend for rr rides and gg games. What is the total, in dollars, for 44 rides and 66 games?
Show a hint
  • The 3r3r counts all the ride money and the 5g5g counts all the game money. Find each, then add.
Show the full solution
The rides cost 3r=3⋅4=123r=3⋅4=12 dollars and the games cost 5g=5⋅6=305g=5⋅6=30 dollars, for a total of 12+30=4212+30=42​. Each rate stays with the count it belongs to, so the 33 never multiplies the games.
Problem
Maria writes the total for a party as 6(t+2)6(t+2), while Jon writes it as 6t+126t+12. They insist both give the same number for the same tt. For t=8t=8, what value do both expressions produce?
Show a hint
  • Evaluate each expression on its own at t=8t=8, and do the grouped one inside first. Do not rewrite one into the other.
Show the full solution
Maria's 6(t+2)=6⋅10=606(t+2)=6⋅10=60, and Jon's 6t+12=48+12=606t+12=48+12=60, so both give 6060​. Matching at one value is a good sign but not proof, since two expressions can agree at one tt and split at the next.
Key idea
Two expressions are equivalent when they give the same value for every value of the variable. A single matching value, like Maria and Jon's 6060, does not prove equivalence, since two expressions can agree at one input and differ at the next. A single mismatch disproves it. Chapter 2 gives the rules for rewriting one form into another, so for now you check equivalence by evaluating, not by rearranging.
Problem
It is tempting to treat 3(n+4)3(n+4) and 3n+43n+4 as the same expression, but they are not. At n=2n=2, by how much do their values differ?
Show a hint
  • Evaluate both at n=2n=2, the grouped one first, then subtract the smaller from the larger.
  • One value that disagrees is enough to prove two expressions are not the same.
Show the full solution
At n=2n=2, 3(n+4)=3⋅6=183(n+4)=3⋅6=18 while 3n+4=6+4=103n+4=6+4=10, so they differ by 88​. One disagreeing value is enough to prove two expressions are not the same, and that gap of 88 shows up at every nn.
Problem
A parking garage charges $6$6 to enter plus $4$4 for every hour parked, but the first hour is validated free, so you pay for one fewer hour than you stay. The charge for staying hh hours is 6+4(h−1)6+4(h−1) dollars. What do you pay, in dollars, for staying 99 hours?
Show a hint
  • The 66 is a flat entry charge that is not multiplied by anything. The 4(h−1)4(h−1) is the hourly charge on the hours you actually pay for.
  • With one hour free, staying 99 hours means paying for 88 of them.
Show the full solution
Nine hours means paying for h−1=8h−1=8 of them, so the hourly part is 4⋅8=324⋅8=32 dollars, and the flat 66 is added on top for 6+32=386+32=38​. The 66 sits outside the multiplication, so it never gets multiplied by the hours.
Fun fact
Letters for unknowns are younger than the algebra that uses them. François Viète, around 15911591, was the first to use letters for known and unknown quantities alike, and Descartes later fixed the habit we still keep, early letters like a,b,ca,b,c for known numbers and late ones like x,yx,y for unknowns.

This lesson added seven words to your working vocabulary. A variable is a letter that represents a number. An expression is a set of instructions that may use variables. Its terms are the pieces split by ++ and −−, and each term's coefficient is its signed numeric factor. Factors are what multiply inside a term. A constant is a term with no variable. Equivalent expressions agree at every value. Next, 1.5 turns to exponents, the shorthand for repeated multiplication.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Terms are the pieces of an expression separated by ++ and −− signs. How many terms are in 4a+3−b4a+3−b?
Show the solution
The pieces are 4a4a, 33, and −b−b, so there are 33​.
Practice
In 7−4xy7−4xy, what is the coefficient of the term xyxy, sign included?
Show the solution
The term is −4xy−4xy, so its numerical factor, sign and all, is −4−4​. The minus belongs to the term, which makes it part of the coefficient too.
Practice
A taxi charges $4$4 to start plus $2$2 for each mile, so a ride of mm miles costs 4+2m4+2m dollars. What does an 88-mile ride cost, in dollars?
Show the solution
The mileage part is 2⋅8=162⋅8=16 dollars on top of the flat 44, so the cost is 4+16=204+16=20​.
Practice
A theater fills its rows by a fixed rule. Row 11 seats 66, row 22 seats 1010, and row 33 seats 1414, each row adding the same number of seats. How many seats are in row 2020?
Show the solution
Each row adds 44 seats, so row rr seats 2+4r2+4r, since row 11 gives 2+4=62+4=6. Row 2020 seats 2+4⋅20=822+4⋅20=82​.
Practice
The constant term of an expression is the term with no variable. What is the constant term of 9x−5+2x29x−5+2x2?
Show the solution
Only −5−5 has no variable, and the sign stays with it, so the constant term is −5−5​.
Practice
Recall that 3n3n means 33 times nn, while 3+n3+n means 33 plus nn. At n=5n=5, how much larger is 3n3n than 3+n3+n?
Show the solution
At n=5n=5, the product 3n=153n=15 and the sum 3+n=83+n=8, so the product leads by 15−8=715−8=7​.
Practice
The expressions 4(n+3)4(n+3) and 4n+34n+3 are not equal. At n=1n=1, by how much do their values differ?
Show the solution
At n=1n=1, 4(n+3)=4⋅4=164(n+3)=4⋅4=16 while 4n+3=4+3=74n+3=4+3=7, so they differ by 99​. One disagreeing value proves two expressions are not the same, and this gap of 99 holds at every nn.
Practice
The expression 5a+3b5a+3b counts two things at once. Find its value when a=7a=7 and b=3b=3.
Show the solution
Here 5a=355a=35 and 3b=93b=9, so 5a+3b=35+9=445a+3b=35+9=44​.
Practice
Evaluate 10−2(m+1)10−2(m+1) when m=3m=3, keeping the order of operations in mind.
Show the solution
Inside the parentheses, m+1=4m+1=4, then 2⋅4=82⋅4=8, and 10−8=210−8=2​. Subtracting the 22 from the 1010 first would ignore the grouping and give the wrong value.
Practice
Three expressions sit side by side, 2(n+3)2(n+3), 2n+32n+3, and 2n+62n+6. Two of them are equivalent, giving the same value for every nn, and one is the odd one out. Test all three at n=4n=4, and enter the value that the two equivalent ones share.
Show the solution
At n=4n=4 the three values are 2(4+3)=142(4+3)=14, 2⋅4+3=112⋅4+3=11, and 2⋅4+6=142⋅4+6=14, so the shared value is 1414​. The odd one out is 2n+32n+3, while 2(n+3)2(n+3) and 2n+62n+6 agree at every nn, as Chapter 2 will show.
